chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from al-Hasan ibn Sabbah from 'Isa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
"Beware of associating with the common people (al-safala), for indeed the common people do not lead to good."

key_terms.السَّفِلَةِ: The common people; ordinary folks, often contrasted with the learned or pious
key_terms.يَئُولُ إِلَى: Leads to; results in; returns to

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'al-safala' mean in Shia hadith and why should one be cautious in associating with them?
ai.summary: In the context of commercial ethics within *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against the social influence of *al-safala* (the common people), a term in Shia scholarship often denoting those lacking deep religious insight or piety. This advice underscores the principle that prolonged association with the spiritually ungrounded can dilute one's own religious commitment and moral standing, thereby impacting the integrity of trade and daily conduct.
